questions.q: Banks handling lakhs of cheque and transaction records centrally typically deploy:
questions.solution: Mainframes (e.g. IBM zSeries) are built for very high-volume, reliable, simultaneous transaction processing - exactly banking, railways and census workloads.
questions.shortcut: Bulk transactions -> mainframe; raw scientific speed -> supercomputer; one appliance control -> embedded/microcontroller.

questions.q: Which of the following is a private IP address commonly used by home routers?
questions.solution: 192.168.0.0/16 is reserved for private networks - the default address of most home routers. 172.32 lies outside the private 172.16-172.31 block, 169.254.x.x is APIPA/link-local, and 8.8.8.8 is Google's public DNS.
questions.shortcut: The private trio: 10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x. Everything else is public.

questions.q: The default file extension of a workbook created in MS Excel 2019 is:
questions.solution: Excel 2007 onwards saves workbooks as .xlsx (Office Open XML). .xls is the 97-2003 format, .xlsm is macro-enabled, .ods is OpenDocument.
questions.shortcut: X = XML = 2007+ across all Office extensions.

questions.q: Who is known as the first computer programmer for her notes on the Analytical Engine?
questions.solution: Ada Lovelace wrote the first published algorithm intended for Charles Babbage's Analytical Engine, making her the first programmer. Grace Hopper pioneered COBOL and coined 'debugging'.
questions.shortcut: Ada = first program (on paper); Hopper = COBOL + debugging. Don't swap them.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the sentence: 'They will cancel the match if it rains.'
options: The match will be cancel if it rains.
The match will be cancelled if it rains.
The match would be cancelled if it rains.
The match will been cancelled if it rains.
questions.solution: Future row: **will be + V3** — *The match will be cancelled if it rains.* The vague *they* disappears; the if-clause stays untouched. 'Will be cancel' lacks the participle; 'would be cancelled' downgrades the modal; 'will been cancelled' breaks the slot (been never follows a bare modal).
questions.shortcut: Modal row: modal + be + V3. Nothing between modal and be.

questions.q: Select the correct active form of the sentence: 'The old bridge has been declared unsafe.'
options: They had declared the old bridge unsafe.
They have declared the old bridge unsafe.
They has declared the old bridge unsafe.
They are declaring the old bridge unsafe.
questions.solution: has been + V3 → present perfect with the vague doer: **They have declared the old bridge unsafe.** 'Had declared' shifts to past perfect; 'has declared' fails to agree with they; 'are declaring' changes the aspect.
questions.shortcut: has/have been + V3 → they have + V3.

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

The old man said, "I bought this house forty years ago."
options: The old man said that he had bought that house forty years ago.
The old man said that he bought that house forty years before.
The old man said that he had bought this house forty years before.
The old man said that he had bought that house forty years before.
questions.solution: bought steps to **had bought**, this → **that**, and ago → **before**. 'Forty years ago' measures from a day that is no longer the reference point; 'he bought' leaves the verb on the direct rung; 'this house' keeps the speaker's pointing word.
questions.shortcut: ago → before; this → that; V2 → had + V3. All three.

questions.q: Select the correct passive form of the question: 'Who invented the radio?'
options: By whom the radio was invented?
By whom was the radio invented?
questions.solution: Who as doer → **By whom + auxiliary + subject + V3**: *By whom was the radio invented?* 'By whom the radio was invented?' is statement order — the auxiliary must precede the subject in a question; 'Who was the radio invented' scrambles the roles.
questions.shortcut: Who-questions: By whom + aux + subject + V3 + ?

questions.q: Which film won Best Picture at the 98th Academy Awards (2026)?
questions.solution: ***One Battle After Another*** (Paul Thomas Anderson) won Best Picture; Anderson also won Best Director, with the film taking six awards overall.
questions.shortcut: Oscars 2026 sweep: One Battle After Another = 6 awards.

questions.q: Digboi, the site of India's oldest oil refinery, is located in which state?
questions.solution: The **Digboi** refinery in **Assam** began operating in **1901** and is the oldest operating refinery in India. Gujarat has Ankleshwar and Koyali; Mumbai High is an offshore field off Maharashtra.

questions.q: Towering gateways called **gopurams** are a characteristic feature of which temple style?
questions.solution: In the **Dravida** style the sanctum is topped by a pyramidal **vimana**, and later temples have huge **gopurams** in the enclosure walls (e.g. Meenakshi temple, Madurai). Nagara temples have a curved shikhara and no gopuram.

questions.q: Who first discovered the cell, in 1665?
questions.solution: **Robert Hooke** observed box-like compartments in a thin slice of **cork** in 1665 and called them 'cells'. Robert Brown discovered the nucleus (1831) and Leeuwenhoek first saw living cells.

questions.q: An alloy of 40 grams contains zinc and copper in the ratio 5 : 3. How much copper must be added so that the ratio becomes 5 : 7?
questions.solution: Zinc 25 g, copper 15 g. Want $\frac{25}{15 + x} = \frac{5}{7}$ ⇒ $15 + x = 35$ ⇒ $x = 20$ g.
questions.shortcut: Zinc constant 25; copper must reach 35 ⇒ add 20 g.

questions.q: What is the unit digit of $7^{105} - 3^{58}$?
questions.solution:
$105 \bmod 4 = 1$ → $7^{105}$ ends in 7.
$58 \bmod 4 = 2$ → $3^{58}$ ends in 9.
$7 - 9$ is negative, so borrow: $17 - 9 = 8$. Unit digit **8**.
questions.shortcut: Trap 2 comes from doing 9 − 7. The first number is bigger, so borrow 10.

questions.q: Find the value of $105^2 - 95^2$.
questions.shortcut: Trap 19,900: computing both squares fully and mis-subtracting is slow and error-prone.

questions.solution: Denominator is $a^2 - ab + b^2$, so the numerator factors as $(a+b)(a^2-ab+b^2)$. Value $= a + b = 2.7 + 3.3 = 6$.

questions.shortcut: Fix the most distinctive stroke (a lone diagonal or an odd-length line), locate it in the main figure, then check the rest.

questions.q: **P is 11th from the left end and Q is 9th from the right end of a row of 30 people. How many people are between them?**
questions.solution: Opposite ends: $30 - 11 - 9$ = **10** between.

questions.q: Select the related word: **Hygrometer : Humidity :: Ammeter : ?**
questions.solution: A hygrometer measures humidity, so the link is instrument : quantity measured. An **ammeter measures current**. Voltage goes with a voltmeter and resistance with an ohmmeter; 'electricity' is too vague.

questions.q: Select the set in which the numbers are related in the same way as the numbers of the following sets. (Operations on whole numbers only.) **(14, 5, 9)** and **(20, 8, 12)**
questions.solution: The **first number = second + third**: 5 + 9 = 14 and 8 + 12 = 20. Test: 9 + 8 = 17 ✓. The others give 16, 11 and 24. **Answer: (17, 9, 8).**
